newsitem.title: FRANCE: Analysts up southwest central French grain yields.
newsitem.headline: Analysts up southwest central French grain yields.

text.p: With the grain harvest over in southwest central France, crop analysts in the Poitou-Charentes region are revising up estimates of wheat and barley yields.
"It is a good crop in terms of both quality and quantity," an analyst for the local ONIC grain office told Reuters.
The wheat crop initially suffered from a prolonged spring drought but early July showers helped it to recover.
The barley crop largely escaped the drought, he said.
The local wheat yield is now expected to reach 6.1 tonnes per hectare, against 5.7 tonnes forecast in mid-July and 5.6 tonnes last year.
Barley yields have been revised up to six tonnes from 5.6 tonnes in mid-July and 4.7 tonnes last year.
Rapeseed yields are put at 3.5-3.7 tonnes against 3.2-3.3 tonnes last year, in line with previous estimates.
The Poitou-Charentes region stretches from the Atlantic coast to the western part of the Loire valley and produces five percent of the barley harvest and seven percent of the wheat.
ONIC expects the region's wheat sowings to jump 14 percent to 358,500 hectares and barley sowings nine percent to 88,700 hectares this year.
Initial results suggest good wheat and barley quality, analysts said.
Wheat was producing protein of 10.5-12 percent and specific weights of 78-81 kg per hectolitre against 74-78 forecast in mid-July.
Hagberg values of 250-320 are reported in line with the requirements for bread-making wheat.
Barley had protein contents of 10.5 percent in the Vienne area and of 11-11.5 percent in the Charentes region, close to the levels requested by the malting industry.
